sources: key owners the spec cites unquoted: E32-D01 §5.3 (D01:111-130), E30-D02 §14 (E30:369-460) and D15-D16 (E30:140-141)
spec §3.2 L158-171 (the native-stop floor, one treatment)
spec §3.4 L184-200 (entry modes, recompute lines, rounding)
spec §3.3 L173-182 (four classes, one sentence each)
spec §0 L35-74 (page, 13 boards, 73 frames, names, PNGs, build order)
copy_gaps: Rows 5 and 26: the recompute line, the risk read-out and slippage describe a valid stop; the rows give no figures for a wrong-side value (64,050.0; 63,990.0), so none is drawn (no number derived).
Row 5: TP 1's R and profit at the typed 63,990.0 are not given: TP 1 shows the unit word 'price' and its quantity 0.062 (§4.1 L338) only.

Row 26: the short's liq, leverage, R now, risk read-out, slippage, take-profit rungs, trail and breakeven are not given: not drawn (the frame runs header, read-out, stop row, CMP-158 note, footer). Its TP side line (sltp.v.tp_side, short) is not drawn either. The spec disagrees with itself here: Validation in situ (L409: 'under the stop field and under TP 1 (rows 5 and 26, long and short)') and row 26's 'row 5 mirrored' (L387) ask for it, while row 26's When and Copy column type and name only the stop (L387) and §3.8 L283 lists sltp.v.tp_side for SCR-064 row 5 only. The spec gives no TP 1 value for the short, so the line cannot be drawn without a derived number; the board follows the narrower reading. Open for the spec text: give row 26 TP 1's typed value (the board then draws the ladder with 'Take-profit must be below the last price (64,011.0) for a short.' under TP 1), or reword L409 to 'under the stop field (rows 5 and 26, long and short) and under TP 1 (row 5)' (no board change).

Row 26: E30-D02's v.summary.heading "Can't submit — {n} problems" (E30:384) has no singular, so row 26's one-problem summary would read 'Can't submit — 1 problems'; the frame shows the moment before Apply and the annotation names the summary.

Row 5: E32 quotes no summary link string; the two links follow E30-D02's 'Field: message' form (E30:308) with the anatomy's field names, 'Stop-loss' (sl.label's first segment, §4.1 L329) and 'TP 1' (L338), before row 5's two messages (L386).

Rows 5, 26, 7 and 8: Apply's validity hold carries no reason line. The rows (L386-L390) and §3.6 L250-L251 name none and §3.8 has no key for it; E30-D02 D16's submit is CMP-001 disabled-with-reason with v.submit.reason 'Fix {n} problems to submit' under it (E30:385), which has no singular (rows 26, 7 and 8 would read 'Fix 1 problems to submit') and says 'submit' on an Apply. Every control is a composition from tokens, named '<CMP id> <Name> (composition)': the wireframes are greys only, and cvsheet v1 cannot recolour an instance or swap its glyph.
A focus ring is a 2 px inner stroke on a wrapper with space.inset.xs padding, so it sits 2 px off the control and adds 4 px on each side to the layout (CMP-039).

Segmented controls draw the anatomy's words verbatim, the selected one in capitals as written (BUY, LIMIT; §5.1 L458, §6.1 L628) and marked by the selected fill; the unit switch's '*' (L330) is that fill.
A validity hold (§3.6 L250-252: 'the host's call') is drawn as the control's own look with its reason as a description and no lock glyph: the spec does not draw it.
Frame captions, annotation labels, board titles, source lines and footers are board chrome, not product copy.
1 px outlines use cvlib's default stroke (1 px, inner) without binding border.hairline; 2 px boundaries and rings bind border.thick / border.focus (frames stay small: FRAME_NOTE).

Modal sizes are kit choices (the spec gives none): SCR-064 640 px wide, SCR-065 800 px (its minimum width 640 px collapses notional and cum. notional, §5.2 L519), SCR-069 720 px; heights hug the content except the 50-row frame (12 body rows, §5.2 L527).
No close (×) control is drawn in the dialog headers: §3.1 L152 names the verb, the object and the environment pill only; Esc closes (L151).

Every number is JetBrains Mono (§3.1 L155) in fields, cells, tiles and the read-out pairs; a number inside a sentence keeps the sentence's Inter, because a cvsheet v1 text node carries one typography.

Frames are named 'SCR-0xx / <state>' (§0 L47), and cvsheet splits section paths on '/', so no section can address a node inside a frame: every frame is rendered whole in one section (the kit keeps each under 24000 bytes; one over the 12000-byte budget is listed in live_checks).
